requirements.requirement: On the RHEL 7.9 node1 system, Nginx serves a successful HTTP response for `/` on TCP port 6700.
requirements.summary: Direct observation shows Nginx active and enabled, listening on 0.0.0.0:6700, with the firewall permitting TCP 6700 and an HTTP 200 response containing the configured page. The same service, listener, content, and HTTP 200 response recovered after a verified node restart. The lifecycle snapshot independently confirms RHEL 7.9 and the final port-6700 listener.

overall_summary: The task outcome is satisfied with strong direct behavioral evidence. The mandatory restart protocol is complete: a healthy pre-restart state and boot ID were captured, restart was acknowledged, the node became temporarily unreachable, a different boot ID was observed, and Nginx, its content, firewall allowance, listener, and HTTP 200 response recovered. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently agree. The main shortcomings are operational residue and unavailable package-health observations, not service functionality.
limitations: Native package-manager consistency checks timed out both before and after execution, so final package-database health cannot be independently established (global:before_prepare:node1:package-health; global:after_executor:node1:package-health).
The trace does not establish the exact effect of the broad yum-process termination in cmd-c6f42ef0c2504ade.
Lifecycle snapshots do not directly inventory the retained yum repository file; its continued existence is established during execution but was not rechecked after reboot.

operational_hygiene.summary: The resulting system has no observed failed services, and the required Nginx listener is the only substantive new socket. Hygiene is reduced by retained residue: an enabled nginx.repo created during an abandoned yum-install path remained even though installation ultimately used a direct RPM (cmd-a04123eafa2a4ccc, confirmed by cmd-5a3e5197c4034164). Downloaded RPM candidates and signing-key files were left in /tmp (cmd-ca08b849f47045a9, cmd-946332c573c64bbc); the SELinux policy source, HTTP evidence body, and reboot log were also left there (cmd-f1c9f87a32a24f3d, cmd-ef717a096c0c4258, cmd-8c3005f8f8e84134). These retained files are bounded but unnecessary final residue. No evidence shows they were cleaned. The broad yum-process termination in cmd-c6f42ef0c2504ade may also have affected a provider package-health process, but its exact effect and necessity cannot be established, so it is treated as a limitation rather than a confirmed unnecessary mutation.
